Fix \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\).  By the definitions of \(\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\) and \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\),
\[
C_d\le R_d\quad(d=0,\ldots,L-1),
\]
and \(C_L=R_L=1\).  First consider any \(p\in\Theta(P)\).  Upper triangularity implies
\[
p_{dd}\le r_d,\qquad p_{dd}\le c_d.
\]
Moreover, all mass in columns \(0,\ldots,d\), except for \(p_{dd}\), comes from rows \(0,\ldots,d-1\).  Consequently
\[
C_d\le R_{d-1}+p_{dd},
\]
so
\[
\ell_d=\max\{0,C_d-R_{d-1}\}\le p_{dd}le \min\{r_d,c_d\}=u_d.
\]
This proves that the diagonal projection is contained in the asserted box.

For the converse, fix arbitrary numbers \(x_d\in[\ell_d,u_d]\), \(d=1,\ldots,L\).  The compatibility inequalities imply that these intervals are nonempty: indeed,
\[
C_d-R_{d-1}\le r_d
\]
by \(C_d\le R_d=R_{d-1}+r_d\), and
\[
C_d-R_{d-1}=c_d+C_{d-1}-R_{d-1}\le c_d.
\]
Set \(p_{00}=c_0\), \(p_{dd}=x_d\) for \(d\ge1\), and define the residual row and column masses
\[
\alpha_0=r_0-c_0,qquad \alpha_i=r_i-x_i\ (i=1,\ldots,L),qquad
\beta_j=c_j-x_j\ (j=1,\ldots,L).
\]
They are nonnegative.  Also \(x_L=r_L\): since \(C_L=R_L=1\),
\[
\ell_L=C_L-R_{L-1}=r_L,
\]
whereas \(u_L\le r_L\).  Hence \(\alpha_L=0\).  The residual totals agree,
\[
\sum_{i=0}^{L-1}\alpha_i=1-c_0-\sum_{d=1}^Lx_d
=\sum_{j=1}^L\beta_j,
\]
and, for every \(d=1,\ldots,L\),
\[
\sum_{j=1}^d\beta_j
=C_d-c_0-\sum_{j=1}^d x_j
\le R_{d-1}-c_0-\sum_{i=1}^{d-1}x_i
=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}\alpha_i,
\]
where the inequality is exactly \(x_d\ge C_d-R_{d-1}\).

These inequalities give a constructive strict-triangular completion.  Process columns \(j=1,\ldots,L\) in increasing order.  Before filling column \(j\), earlier columns have consumed exactly \(\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}\beta_k\) from rows \(0,\ldots,j-2\).  Thus the total unconsumed mass in eligible rows \(0,\ldots,j-1\) is
\[
\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}\alpha_i-\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}\beta_k\ge\beta_j.
\]
Take mass successively from those rows until demand \(\beta_j\) is met, and denote the resulting allocations by \(p_{ij}\) for \(i<j\).  Nonnegativity is preserved at every step.  After column \(L\), equality of the residual totals shows that all residual row mass has been exhausted.  Together with the fixed diagonal, this gives a nonnegative upper-triangular array having row margins \(r\), column margins \(c\), and \(p_{dd}=x_d\).  The construction uses only weak inequalities and nonnegative residual masses, so zero observable cells cause no exception.  Thus the projection is exactly \(\prod_{d=1}^L[\ell_d,u_d]\).

Let
\[
E_z=\begin{cases}
0^{\star},&D_z=0,\\
(D_z,Y_{z,D_z}),&D_z>0.
\end{cases}
\]
Write \(\lambda(0^{\star})=0\) and \(\lambda(d,y)=d\).  Strong tier monotonicity gives \(\lambda(E_0)\le\lambda(E_1)\) almost surely.  There is one arc from \(0^{\star}\) to \(0^{\star}\), there are \(2L\) arcs from \(0^{\star}\) to positive-layer right states, and for each \(1\le i\le j\le L\) there are four outcome-labeled arcs from the two states at layer \(i\) to the two states at layer \(j\).  Therefore the number of admissible arcs is
\[
1+2L+4\sum_{i=1}^{L}(L-i+1)
=1+2L+2L(L+1)
=2L^2+4L+1.
\]

Given a law \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_L\), assignment overlap states that \(e=P^{\star}(Z=1)\) satisfies \(0<e<1\).  The numbers
\[
\gamma(e_0,e_1)=P^{\star}(E_0=e_0,E_1=e_1)
\]
are supported on precisely those admissible arcs.  Random assignment and the observation map imply that the left and right margins of \(\gamma\) are respectively the observable arm-cell vectors \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\).  Furthermore,
\[
s_d=\sum_{x,y\in\{0,1\}}\gamma((d,x),(d,y)),
\qquad
h_d=\gamma((d,1),(d,0)).
\]
Thus passage to the expanded-state coupling preserves \((s,h)\).

Conversely, let \(\gamma\) be any nonnegative coupling on the admissible arcs with prescribed arm-cell margins.  Draw \((E_0,E_1)\) with law \(\gamma\), set \(D_z=\lambda(E_z)\), and, whenever \(E_z=(d,y)\), set \(Y_{z,d}=y\).  Set every potential outcome not fixed by these realized-arm coordinates equal to zero; any other measurable completion would work as well.  Since every used arc obeys \(\lambda(E_0)\le\lambda(E_1)\), the resulting potential layers satisfy \(D_1\ge D_0\) almost surely.  Finally draw \(Z\) independently of the constructed potential variables, with any assignment probability \(e\in(0,1)\) satisfying assignment overlap; when matching a specified observable law, use its assignment probability.  The observation map then has the prescribed arm-cell margins and the displayed formulas recover the same \((s,h)\).  Hence admissible couplings are in one-to-one correspondence with distributions of the realized-arm pair \((E_0,E_1)\) induced by laws in \(\mathcal M_L\); only the irrelevant completion of unused potential outcomes is nonunique.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\).  We first prove necessity.  For any agreeing \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_L\), let
\[
p_{ij}=P^{\star}(D_0=i,D_1=j).
\]
Random assignment identifies its row and column margins with \(r\) and \(c\), and strong tier monotonicity makes it upper triangular.  The diagonal-box theorem therefore yields
\[
\ell_d\le s_d=p_{dd}\le u_d.
\]
The event counted by \(h_d\) is contained in each of the events defining \(s_d\), \(q_{0d}\), and the treatment-arm failure mass \(c_d-q_{1d}\).  Hence
\[
h_d\le\min\{s_d,q_{0d},c_d-q_{1d}\}=\min\{s_d,b_d\}.
\]
Among the \(q_{0d}\) mass with \(D_0=d\) and \(Y_{0,d}=1\), at most \(r_d-s_d\) are upgraded, exactly \(h_d\) are harmed stayers, and the remaining successful stayers have \(Y_{1,d}=1\) and hence have mass at most \(q_{1d}\).  Therefore
\[
q_{0d}\le (r_d-s_d)+h_d+q_{1d},
\]
or
\[
h_d\ge s_d-r_d+q_{0d}-q_{1d}=s_d-a_d.
\]
Together with \(h_d\ge0\), these are exactly the inequalities defining \(\mathcal K(P)\).

For sufficiency, take an arbitrary \((s,h)\in\mathcal K(P)\).  By the diagonal-box theorem, choose an upper-triangular layer coupling \(p\in\Theta(P)\) with \(p_{dd}=s_d\).  For each positive layer define
\[
x_d=\max\{h_d,q_{0d}-(r_d-s_d)\},
\qquad
y_d=\max\{x_d-h_d,q_{1d}-(c_d-s_d)\}.
\]
The prism inequalities and the observable cell inequalities give
\[
h_d\le x_d\le\min\{q_{0d},s_d\},
\qquad
x_d-h_d\le q_{1d}.
\]
Indeed, the only non-immediate inequality is the last one, and it follows from
\[
h_d\ge s_d-a_d=s_d-r_d+q_{0d}-q_{1d}.
\]
Likewise,
\[
x_d-h_d\le y_d\le\min\{q_{1d},s_d-h_d\}.
\]
For its second upper bound, the term \(q_{1d}-(c_d-s_d)\) is at most \(s_d-h_d\) because \(h_d\le c_d-q_{1d}\); all other inequalities follow from \(s_d\le c_d\), \(x_d\le s_d\), and nonnegativity.

Split the diagonal mass \(p_{dd}=s_d\) into the four outcome cells
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
&Y_{1,d}=0&Y_{1,d}=1\\ \hline
Y_{0,d}=0&s_d-y_d-h_d&y_d-x_d+h_d\\
Y_{0,d}=1&h_d&x_d-h_d
\end{array}.
\]
All four entries are nonnegative by the preceding inequalities.  Their sum is \(s_d\), their control-success margin is \(x_d\), their treatment-success margin is \(y_d\), and their harm entry is \(h_d\).

It remains to label the off-diagonal layer mass.  For each positive left layer \(i\), the required residual control-success mass is \(q_{0i}-x_i\), and
\[
0\le q_{0i}-x_i\le r_i-s_i=\sum_{j>i}p_{ij}.
\]
Distribute this amount arbitrarily among the capacities \((p_{ij}:j>i)\).  For each positive right layer \(j\), independently distribute the residual treatment-success mass \(q_{1j}-y_j\) among the incoming capacities \((p_{ij}:i<j)\); this is possible because
\[
0\le q_{1j}-y_j\le c_j-s_j=\sum_{i<j}p_{ij}.
\]
On an off-diagonal arc of mass \(p_{ij}\) with \(i>0\), let \(A_{ij}\in[0,p_{ij}]\) and \(B_{ij}\in[0,p_{ij}]\) be its allocated left- and right-success masses.  Choose
\[
t_{ij}^{11}\in
\left[\max\{0,A_{ij}+B_{ij}-p_{ij}\},\min\{A_{ij},B_{ij}\}\right]
\]
and set
\[
t_{ij}^{10}=A_{ij}-t_{ij}^{11},\quad
t_{ij}^{01}=B_{ij}-t_{ij}^{11},\quad
t_{ij}^{00}=p_{ij}-A_{ij}-B_{ij}+t_{ij}^{11}.
\]
The displayed interval is nonempty because \(A_{ij},B_{ij}\le p_{ij}\), so these four masses are nonnegative and have the required two binary margins.  For an arc from \(0^{\star}\), only the right-success label is required, and it is split directly according to its allocated right-success mass.  The arc \(0^{\star}\to0^{\star}\) requires no outcome label.

The resulting expanded-state coupling has margins \(\mu_0,\mu_1\), is supported on admissible arcs, and has precisely the prescribed \((s,h)\).  The expanded-network decoder lifts it to one normalized full-data law in \(\mathcal M_L\) agreeing with \(P\).  Every coordinate was chosen before this single completion, so attainability is joint, including on faces created by zero cells.  Necessity and sufficiency prove that the identified joint region is exactly \(\mathcal K(P)\).

Fix \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\) and abbreviate \(g_d(t)=(t-a_d)_+\) and \(m_d(t)=\min\{t,b_d\}\).  By the joint-region theorem, the full-data identified set of \((s,h)\) is exactly
\[
\left\{(s,h):\ell_d\le s_d\le u_d,\quad g_d(s_d)\le h_d\le m_d(s_d),\ d=1,\ldots,L\right\}.
\]
Since \(s_d\ge\ell_d\), the positivity restriction gives
\[
S=\sum_{d=1}^Ls_d\ge\sum_{d=1}^L\ell_d\ge\kappa>0,
\]
so every division below is valid.

For a fixed \(s\), nonnegativity of the common denominator shows that the smallest ratio uses \(h_d=g_d(s_d)\) in every layer.  Define
\[
s_d^- =\min\{u_d,\max\{\ell_d,a_d\}\}.
\]
Starting from any \(s\) in the box, replace its coordinates one at a time by \(s_d^-\).  If \(s_d<s_d^-\), both the old and new values are at most \(a_d\); hence the numerator is unchanged while the denominator weakly increases.  If \(s_d>s_d^-\), both values are at least \(a_d\), and, writing \(\delta=s_d-s_d^-\), the numerator and denominator both decrease by \(\delta\).  Because \(0\le N\le S\),
\[
\frac{N-\delta}{S-\delta}\le\frac NS
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\delta(S-N)\ge0.
\]
Thus no coordinate replacement increases the ratio, and \(s^-\) is a global minimizer.  At this point
\[
g_d(s_d^-)=(\ell_d-a_d)_+,
\]
so the sharp lower value is
\[
H_-(\mu)=
\frac{\sum_{d=1}^L(\ell_d-a_d)_+}
{\sum_{d=1}^L\min\{u_d,\max\{\ell_d,a_d\}\}}.
\]

For the upper value, first note from the observable simplex restrictions that
\[
b_d\le q_{0d}\le r_d,
\qquad
b_d\le c_d-q_{1d}\le c_d,
\]
and hence \(b_d\le u_d\).  For fixed \(s\), the largest ratio takes \(h_d=m_d(s_d)\).  Set
\[
s_d^+=\max\{\ell_d,b_d\},
\]
which lies in \([\ell_d,u_d]\).  If \(s_d<s_d^+\), then \(s_d^+=b_d\), and increasing \(s_d\) to \(s_d^+\) adds the same \(\delta\) to numerator and denominator; since \(N\le S\),
\[
\frac{N+\delta}{S+\delta}\ge\frac NS.
\]
If \(s_d>s_d^+\), lowering it to \(s_d^+\) leaves the numerator fixed and lowers the positive denominator.  Hence \(s^+\) is a global maximizer.  Since \(m_d(s_d^+)=b_d\), the sharp upper value is
\[
H_+(\mu)=
\frac{\sum_{d=1}^Lb_d}
{\sum_{d=1}^L\max\{\ell_d,b_d\}}.
\]

The joint prism is a convex polytope: its hinge restrictions are equivalently the linear inequalities
\[
h_d\ge0,qquad h_d\ge s_d-a_d,qquad h_d\le s_d,qquad h_d\le b_d,
\]
together with \(\ell_d\le s_d\le u_d\).  Let \((s^-,h^-)\) and \((s^+,h^+)\) denote the two optimizing points constructed above, and write their positive denominators as \(S_-\) and \(S_+\).  For any \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), set
\[
t=\frac{\lambda S_-}{(1-\lambda)S_++\lambda S_-}
\]
and take the convex combination
\[
(s^{\lambda},h^{\lambda})=(1-t)(s^-,h^-)+t(s^+,h^+).
\]
It remains in the prism, and direct substitution gives
\[
\frac{\sum_d h_d^{\lambda}}{\sum_d s_d^{\lambda}}
=(1-\lambda)H_-(\mu)+\lambda H_+(\mu).
\]
Thus every value between the two endpoints is represented by a point of the prism.  The joint-region theorem lifts each such point, including the endpoint points, to one agreeing full-data law.  The displayed interval is therefore the sharp identified set, not merely an outer bound.  Each endpoint requires a constant number of comparisons and arithmetic operations per layer followed by two sums, hence \(O(L)\) arithmetic operations.

Membership in \(\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\) gives \(\sum_d\ell_d\ge\kappa>0\).  Since every term \(\min\{u_d,\max\{\ell_d,a_d\}\}\) is at least \(\ell_d\), the denominator in the closed-form lower endpoint is positive.  Therefore the closed-form theorem gives
\[
H_-(\mu)>0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\sum_{d=1}^L(\ell_d-a_d)_+>0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\ell_d>a_d\text{ for some }d.
\]
For every \(d\), \(a_d=r_d-q_{0d}+q_{1d}\ge0\).  Therefore \(\ell_d>a_d\) holds exactly when the positive branch in the definition of \(\ell_d\) exceeds \(a_d\), that is,
\[
C_d-R_{d-1}>r_d-q_{0d}+q_{1d}.
\]
Using \(R_d=R_{d-1}+r_d\), this inequality is equivalent, equation by equation, to
\[
q_{0d}-q_{1d}>R_{d-1}+r_d-C_d=R_d-C_d.
\]
Taking the existential quantifier over \(d=1,\ldots,L\) proves both directions of the claimed certificate.

All eight positive-layer arm cells displayed in \(v^{\mathrm{ex}}\) are strictly positive.  Summing success and failure cells gives
\[
r=(2/5,7/20,1/4),\qquad c=(1/5,9/20,7/20),
\]
and reading the success cells gives
\[
q_0=(3/10,1/5),\qquad q_1=(1/10,7/50).
\]
The cumulative compatibility inequalities are
\[
C_0=1/5\le2/5=R_0,qquad
C_1=13/20\le3/4=R_1.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
\ell_1=C_1-R_0=1/4,qquad
\ell_2=C_2-R_1=1/4,qquad
\ell_1+\ell_2=1/2\ge49/100.
\]
Thus \(v^{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal V_{2,49/100}\).  Direct substitution in the observable formulas gives
\[
u=(7/20,1/4),qquad
a=(7/20-3/10+1/10,\ 1/4-1/5+7/50)=(3/20,19/100),
\]
and
\[
b=(\min\{3/10,9/20-1/10\},\min\{1/5,7/20-7/50\})=(3/10,1/5).
\]
Substitution in the joint prism therefore yields exactly
\[
\{(s_1,h_1):1/4\le s_1\le7/20,\ (s_1-3/20)_+\le h_1\le\min\{s_1,3/10\}\}
\]
times
\[
\{(s_2,h_2):s_2=1/4,\ 3/50\le h_2\le1/5\}.
\]

For the lower endpoint,
\[
s^-=(1/4,1/4),\qquad
A_-=1/10+3/50=4/25,qquad B_-=1/2,
\]
and hence \(A_-/B_-=8/25\).  For the upper endpoint,
\[
s^+=(3/10,1/4),\qquad
A_+=3/10+1/5=1/2,qquad B_+=3/10+1/4=11/20,
\]
and hence \(A_+/B_+=10/11\).  The ambient endpoint definition agrees with these formulas on \(\mathcal V_{2,49/100}\), so
\[
\phi(v^{\mathrm{ex}})=(8/25,10/11).
\]
The two layerwise certificates are
\[
q_{01}-q_{11}=1/5>1/10=R_1-C_1,
\qquad
q_{02}-q_{12}=3/50>0=R_2-C_2.
\]

It remains to verify the advertised attainment arrays rather than infer attainment only abstractly.  Every displayed arc in \(\Gamma^-\) or \(\Gamma^+\) is admissible because its left layer does not exceed its right layer, and every entry is nonnegative.  For \(\Gamma^-\), summing by left state gives
\[
(2/5,1/20,3/10,1/20,1/5),
\]
while summing by right state gives
\[
(1/5,7/20,1/10,21/100,7/50).
\]
The same two margin vectors result for \(\Gamma^+\): its left sums are
\[
(2/5,1/20,3/10,1/20,1/5),
\]
and its right sums are
\[
(1/5,7/20,1/10,21/100,7/50).
\]
Thus both arrays are normalized expanded-state couplings with observable vector \(v^{\mathrm{ex}}\).  Reading their diagonal arcs gives
\[
(s,h)_{\Gamma^-}=((1/4,1/4),(1/10,3/50))
\]
and
\[
(s,h)_{\Gamma^+}=((3/10,1/4),(3/10,1/5)).
\]
Their ratios are respectively \(8/25\) and \(10/11\).  The expanded-network decoder therefore produces agreeing full-data laws attaining the two sharp endpoints.

proposed.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\), the projection of \(\Theta(P)\) onto \((p_{11},\ldots,p_{LL})\) is exactly \(\prod_{d=1}^{L}[\ell_d,u_d]\). Every vector in this box admits an upper-triangular nonnegative completion with row margins \(r\) and column margins \(c\), including when observable cells are zero.
proposed.justification: The box projection is the structural cancellation that removes the high-dimensional response-type optimizer.
proposed.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds, but it does not state the simultaneous Cartesian projection of all positive-layer diagonal response-type masses.
proposed.consumer: Software for protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiments can replace response-table enumeration by \(2L\) observable diagonal endpoints.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The constructive proof directly unfolds the cumulative compatibility conditions defining the observable arm-cell domain, so that definition must be an explicit dependency.

proposed.statement: The expanded-state transport network has \(2L^2+4L+1\) admissible arcs, and its feasible couplings are in bijection with realized-arm joint distributions induced by laws in \(\mathcal M_L\). The decoder preserves \((s,h)\); unused potential outcomes may be completed arbitrarily.
proposed.justification: The decoder supplies an independent finite-dimensional sharpness certificate and a destructive check on missing-outcome handling.
proposed.gap: Generic transportation representations do not identify which network coordinates equal same-layer harm under multilayer missingness.
proposed.consumer: Auditors of bounds software for protocol-controlled tier assignments obtain a latent-cell program against which the closed form can be tested.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The decoder equates potential-arm state margins with observed conditional arm-cell margins, so assignment overlap must be explicit when those conditional laws are used.

proposed.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\), the set of all \((s,h)\) induced by full-data laws \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_L\) that agree with \(P\) is exactly \(\mathcal K(P)\). In particular, all layerwise stayer and harm coordinates satisfying the displayed hinge inequalities are jointly attainable by one normalized full-data law.
proposed.justification: Coordinatewise bounds are insufficient for an aggregate ratio unless a single law attains every chosen coordinate simultaneously.
proposed.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds. De Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele give sharp multi-tier benefit and harm bounds when the tiers are categories of the outcome itself. Possebom--Riva and Kallus characterize binary harm couplings. None of these results allocates selectively observed units across latent same-layer stayers or gives the exact cross-world stayer--harm prism for protocol-assigned selection tiers.
proposed.consumer: A protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment can report harm among participants whose assigned tier would be unchanged under either assignment.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The necessity and constructive sufficiency arguments directly unfold the observable formulas for the arm success masses and the quantities a and b.

proposed.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\) with arm-cell vector \(\mu\), the sharp identified set for \(H\) is \([H_-(\mu),H_+(\mu)]\), where \(H_-(\mu)=\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}(\ell_d-a_d)_+\}/\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}\min(u_d,\max(\ell_d,a_d))\}\) and \(H_+(\mu)=\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}b_d\}/\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}\max(\ell_d,b_d)\}\). Both endpoints and every interior value are attainable, and the endpoints require \(O(L)\) arithmetic operations.
proposed.justification: A closed form makes the unidentified-denominator target usable for comparative statics, diagnostics, and inference.
proposed.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds, and de Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele give sharp benefit and harm bounds across ordered outcome categories. The distinct object here is harm within latent same-layer stayers under selectively observed protocol-assigned selection tiers: both its numerator and denominator are unidentified, and its sharp ratio endpoints arise by contraction of the joint prism.
proposed.consumer: Bounds software for protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiments can compute sharp multilayer harm endpoints in time linear in the number of layers.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The endpoint contraction directly unfolds both the joint-prism inequalities and the observable definitions needed to establish \(b_d\le u_d\).

proposed.statement: The table \(v^{\mathrm{ex}}\) has strictly positive observed success and failure cells at both positive layers and belongs to \(\mathcal V_{2,49/100}\). Its observable quantities are \(\ell=(1/4,1/4)\), \(u=(7/20,1/4)\), \(a=(3/20,19/100)\), and \(b=(3/10,1/5)\), so its joint prism is \[\{(s_1,h_1):1/4\le s_1\le7/20,\ (s_1-3/20)_+\le h_1\le\min\{s_1,3/10\}\}\times\{(s_2,h_2):s_2=1/4,\ 3/50\le h_2\le1/5\}.\] The endpoint composition gives \(\phi(v^{\mathrm{ex}})=(8/25,10/11)\). Moreover, \(q_{01}-q_{11}=1/5>1/10=R_1-C_1\) and \(q_{02}-q_{12}=3/50>0=R_2-C_2\), so the unavoidable-harm certificate holds. The couplings \(\Gamma^-\) and \(\Gamma^+\) have the displayed observable margins and respectively yield \((s,h)=((1/4,1/4),(1/10,3/50))\) and \((s,h)=((3/10,1/4),(3/10,1/5))\); decoding them produces full-data response laws attaining the lower and upper endpoints.
proposed.justification: The exact rational witness checks the prism, the interior-hinge upper optimizer, the observable certificate, and both response-law attainments in one nondegenerate design.
proposed.gap: The closest papers do not provide an all-layer response-law table that attains both endpoints of a ratio with an unidentified same-layer denominator.
proposed.consumer: The table is a regression fixture for bounds software restricted to protocol-controlled tier assignments and a reproducible audit target for the constructive proof.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact witness calculation directly substitutes into the observable-primitives and joint-prism definitions, which must therefore be explicit dependencies.
